comment: Every measurable row of PLAN.md section 6, one entry per (id, threshold). Contract 01 section 7.3 owns the comparators. direction records which way is better and release_gate.py asserts it agrees with the comparator.

directions.lower: abs_max and ratio_max rows: a smaller measured value is better
directions.higher: abs_min rows: a larger measured value is better
directions.boolean: bool_true and bool_false rows: the value is a boolean

rows.label: Cold start, median of 10 runs
rows.rule: no worse than the upstream baseline on the same device by more than 5 percent
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/coldstart.sh

rows.label: ANRs during cold start with 76 extensions installed
rows.rule: no ANR at all
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/coldstart.sh --extensions: am_anr entries in the events buffer around each of 10 cold starts, counted by tools/bench/anr_count.py

rows.label: PackageManager or OkHttpClient slices on the main thread during cold start
rows.rule: none at all
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/coldstart.sh --extensions: tools/bench/perfetto_metrics.py --metric main_thread_pm_okhttp_slices on each of 10 cold start traces, summed

rows.label: Webtoon scroll janky frames the application was late for, 4 GB phone
rows.rule: under 1 percent, absolute, about one application-late frame per two swipes. Ruling R40, extended by R50: a frame counts as janky when FrameCompleted minus IntendedVsync, less the SwapBuffers to GpuCompleted wait, is over the frame deadline. The total janky percent and the median GPU wait are recorded in the fragment's method note beside it
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/webtoon_scroll.sh, through tools/bench/framestats.py

rows.label: Webtoon scroll janky frames the application was late for, 2 GB phone
rows.rule: under 1.25 percent, absolute, about three application-late frames per five swipes, the 4 GB tolerance at PLAN.md's 5:4 ratio. Ruling R40, extended by R50: a frame counts as janky when FrameCompleted minus IntendedVsync, less the SwapBuffers to GpuCompleted wait, is over the frame deadline. The total janky percent and the median GPU wait are recorded in the fragment's method note beside it
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/webtoon_scroll.sh, through tools/bench/framestats.py

rows.label: Webtoon scroll janky frames the application was late for, tablet in landscape
rows.rule: under 1 percent, absolute, about one application-late frame per two swipes. Ruling R40, extended by R50: a frame counts as janky when FrameCompleted minus IntendedVsync, less the SwapBuffers to GpuCompleted wait, is over the frame deadline. The total janky percent and the median GPU wait are recorded in the fragment's method note beside it
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/webtoon_scroll.sh with SAIKOU_ORIENTATION=landscape, through tools/bench/framestats.py

rows.label: Page turn janky frames the application was late for, 2 GB phone
rows.rule: under 4 percent, absolute. Ruling R40: a frame counts as janky when FrameCompleted minus IntendedVsync, less the SwapBuffers to GpuCompleted wait, is over the frame deadline. The total janky percent and the median GPU wait are recorded in the fragment's method note beside it
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/page_turn.sh, through tools/bench/framestats.py

rows.label: Peak PSS during a webtoon scroll, 4 GB phone
rows.rule: under 500 MB, absolute
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/meminfo_poll.sh

rows.label: Reader process deaths during the memory window
rows.rule: no crash at all
rows.measuredBy: tools/bench/meminfo_poll.sh

rows.label: Low RAM repro: library covers then a webtoon chapter survive on a 1.5 GB profile
rows.rule: five library passes then a webtoon chapter: same process throughout and no OutOfMemoryError; after every library pass the image memory cache holds at most 25 percent of ActivityManager.memoryClass; live allocation (Java heap in use after a collection plus native heap allocated) after pass 5 at most 5 percent above pass 2
rows.measuredBy: instrumentation fragment, collect.py --instrumentation

rows.label: Download queue intact after a force-stop
rows.rule: the queue is restored exactly
rows.measuredBy: instrumentation fragment; phase 2 pulls it from the 4 GB device in gate.sh step 8b and reads it with collect.py --bench

rows.label: Queue add time with 1,000 downloaded chapters
rows.rule: under 1 second, absolute
rows.measuredBy: instrumentation fragment; phase 2 pulls it from the 4 GB device in gate.sh step 8b and reads it with collect.py --bench

rows.label: Library update of 2,000 entries across 20 sources
rows.rule: a quarter of the upstream baseline on the same device or less; the baseline row is recorded at the start of Phase 2
rows.measuredBy: host bench fragment; gate.sh step 8c runs tools/ci/library_update_rows.sh, which runs tools/bench/library_update.sh saikou 2000x20 (R66) on the 4 GB device and publishes its duration_ms, read with collect.py --bench

rows.label: Library update throughput against the source rate limit
rows.rule: measured requests per second within 10 percent of the RateLimitInterceptor setting
rows.measuredBy: host bench fragment; gate.sh step 8c runs tools/ci/library_update_rows.sh, which runs tools/bench/library_update.sh saikou 500x2 (R66) on the 4 GB device and publishes its min_rate_ratio, read with collect.py --bench

rows.label: Library update cancel latency
rows.rule: under 2 seconds, absolute
rows.measuredBy: instrumentation fragment; phase 2 pulls it from the 4 GB device in gate.sh step 8b and reads it with collect.py --bench

rows.label: Restore of a 3,000 entry backup
rows.rule: under 2 minutes, absolute
rows.measuredBy: instrumentation fragment, collect.py --instrumentation

rows.label: Out of memory errors during the 3,000 entry restore
rows.rule: none at all
rows.measuredBy: instrumentation fragment, collect.py --instrumentation

rows.label: Sync of a 3,000 entry library without running out of memory
rows.rule: the sync completes with no OOM
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_3000.py: SyncPairTest's sync-3000 step on saikou_pixel8a_2g against the sync fixture, its fragment copied to tools/out/bench/pixel8a_2g, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a deleted chapter stays deleted
rows.rule: the tombstone survives a round trip
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a renamed chapter does not duplicate
rows.rule: the url key keeps one row
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a read on one device and an offline bookmark on the other both survive
rows.rule: per field merge keeps both edits
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a fresh device joins with the other's renamed and deleted categories
rows.rule: renamed and deleted categories arrive as they are, one system category, and the first push changes nothing
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a device that restores a backup and then joins keeps both devices' chapters, reads, pages and bookmarks
rows.rule: every chapter of both devices on both, read wherever either read it, the higher page, both bookmarks, and a further sync writes nothing
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: two devices that nest two categories under each other before either syncs show one tree on both
rows.rule: both store the merged cycle and show the same tree, the category with the lower sync key at the top, and a further sync writes nothing
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a category nested under a parent the other device deleted ends at the top level on both
rows.rule: the child shows at the top level on both, no category stores a parent, and a further sync writes nothing
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a device that restores flat categories and then joins keeps the other device's sub-category tree
rows.rule: the restore's flat categories do not flatten the other device's nest on either device, and a further sync writes nothing
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: a title and description edited on one device survive a source refresh on the other, and a reset shows the source's new text on both
rows.rule: both show the edit with the refreshing device's new source title and description under it, a further sync writes nothing, and after the reset both show the source's new text and no edit
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5g, tools/bench/sync_pair.py: SyncPairTest steps on saikou_pixel9_4g and saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: Sync: after 14 idle days and a cold process, the app refreshes its Drive token without asking to sign in (fake token endpoint)
rows.rule: the app's token handling survives idle, process death and transient failure; Google's expiry is owner item 6
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 5h, tools/bench/sync_14_day.py: DriveTokenDeviceTest steps on saikou_api26_2g against the sync fixture's Google endpoints, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench

rows.label: A Saikou export re-imports into upstream v0.20.4 with every field upstream's own backup keeps
rows.rule: UpstreamBackupFieldsTest and UpstreamLosslessExportTest both ran in this gate run and passed
rows.measuredBy: gate.sh step 3b, tools/ci/upstream_lossless_row.sh: :backup:testDebugUnitTest --rerun, this run's JUnit XML, host fragment in tools/out/bench/any, collect.py --bench
